correctness.rationale: Classical rooted-forest counting gives p(n,k)=k/n times the product of (1-j/n); exchangeability gives an exactly uniform conditional k-subset. Its hypergeometric factorial moments and tightness yield the Rayleigh-mixed Poisson limit for early labels. The exact rising factorial moment identity was checked by exhaustive enumeration for n<=6, and its proof gives E[M]~sqrt(pi*n/2), Var(M)=n log n+O(n), and E[M^s]~[s/((s-1)(s-2))]n^(s-1) for each fixed integer s>=3. Specifically the second-moment sum has a half-logarithmic harmonic contribution; for s>=3 the k-series is absolutely summable. Full asymptotic claims follow from these analytic steps; 244 exact computational assertions are finite diagnostics only.

value.rationale: The least labeled cycle point is a canonical discovery-time statistic when scanning a uniformly labeled functional digraph. Its rare-event tail S(t)~t^(-2) causes an exact critical logarithmic variance and an explicit order-(n^(s-1)) hierarchy for all fixed higher integer moments, even though typical first labels lie on the sqrt(n) scale. The Cox limit simultaneously describes every fixed number of early cycle discoveries. These matched results identify a meaningful non-uniform-integrability frontier rather than a routine restatement of the classical core law.
